chunks: 'There is no divorce except when what is intended by it is the divorce.'

key_terms.أُرِيدَ: Intended/willed — the passive form indicating deliberate, conscious intention as a prerequisite for legal validity
key_terms.طلاق: Talaq — the Islamic form of divorce pronounced by the husband; literally 'releasing' or 'untying'

ai.seo_question: In Shia Islam, is a divorce valid if it was not genuinely intended?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that divorce (talaq) is only legally valid when the person uttering it genuinely intends to effect a divorce. This ruling is a foundational principle in Shia Islamic family law: words of divorce spoken in jest, under coercion, or without conscious intention do not constitute a legally binding dissolution of marriage. The ruling addressed a recurring jurisprudential question about the role of sincere intention (niyyah) in legal acts.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no divorce except when what is intended by it is the divorce’.
